claims.text: Infrastructure Australia's 2025 Market Capacity Report (released 13 November 2025) estimates Australia's infrastructure workforce at 204,000 workers as at October 2025 against an estimated shortage of 141,000 workers needed to deliver the five-year Major Public Infrastructure Pipeline, a shortage projected to peak at about 300,000 in 2027, with the pipeline itself up 14% year on year to $242 billion.

sources.title: 2025 Infrastructure Market Capacity Report
sources.whatItMeasured: National audit of workforce, plant and materials capacity against the five-year Major Public Infrastructure Pipeline; workforce size and shortage estimates as at October 2025

claims.scope: Public infrastructure construction nationally, across occupational groups including trades workers and labourers. It measures sector-wide capacity pressure, not demand for first-line supervisors specifically, though sustained delivery pressure is where supervisory hiring concentrates.

claims.text: Reuters reported on 12 August 2026 that Australian residential builders are at capacity limits while pursuing the National Housing Accord target of 1.2 million new homes by 2029, citing official data showing new dwelling commencements fell 11.2% in the first quarter of 2026 compared with the previous quarter, with builders unable to find workers.

sources.title: Australia promised 1.2 million new homes, but builders are at their limits
sources.whatItMeasured: Wire-service reporting combining ABS dwelling commencement statistics for Q1 2026 with firsthand builder accounts of worker scarcity

claims.scope: Residential building nationally. Worker-scarcity anecdotes are attributed to individual builders, not a survey. Says nothing specific about supervisors versus trades, and nothing about AI or automation.
claims.refuteNotes: Lens 1 (source real): major wire service, URL carries dateline 2026-08-12, resolves HTTP 200. Lens 2 (population fit): residential building sector; relevant to this occupation because site supervision scales with active builds, but it is not occupation-specific evidence. Lens 3 (in window): August 2026, inside window. No refuter overturned.
